overview: Taíno names diverse late precolonial Caribbean societies, not every earlier island population. Chiefdoms combined farming, ceremonial life and inter-island connections.

items.text: Wood-and-thatch bohíos differed in size and proximity to ceremonial plazas, reflecting distinctions within chiefdoms.
Communal plazas hosted batey, a team game played with a rubber ball.
Areytos brought storytelling, singing, dancing and drumming together for varied community occasions.
Cemí figures appeared in stone, wood, clay and bone. They carried spiritual significance rather than serving only as decoration.
Canoes connected islands through travel and exchange. Maritime routes were important social links.
Spanish colonization caused profound disruption. Taíno peoples today are revitalizing language and culture.

sources.title: Jose L. Marrero-Rosado, UC Berkeley ORIAS: Tainos and Caribbean Indigenous Peoples
Smithsonian NMAI: Taino Native Heritage and Identity in the Caribbean
